grand_strategy.reading:
Indonesia under Prabowo is the textbook hedger that has chosen to hedge at scale: it has not left the free-and-active line, it has made the line wide enough to hold a BRICS seat, a US defence partnership, a Russian oil contract, an Australian security treaty and Chinese jets at the same time. In Luttwak's terms this is relational manoeuvre rather than alliance: no seam is exploited, because Jakarta sits on all of them, and the point is to make itself too useful to be pushed to either side. The method works while the great powers are in low-grade competition and the bills fall due in different currencies; the Lowy analysis dates its limit to April 2026, when the Iran war closed Hormuz and made energy, not doctrine, decide the week.
The paradoxes are the price of belonging everywhere. Each club costs standing in another: BRICS cost a tariff threat in Washington, the Natuna formula cost the legal case against Beijing, the Board of Peace cost the street at home, the nickel ban cost leverage over its own smelters. The material limits are older than Prabowo: a 3% deficit cap that cannot carry free meals, a capital city and an arsenal at once; a net energy importer; a navy for an archipelago of thousands of islands. The archipelago is Indonesia's strength (everyone needs its straits) and its weakness (no one can be kept out of them).
The grades here follow structure, not courtesy. Almost every great-power relation is partner, because Indonesia treats all of them as purchasable, and the bonds say what the partnerships are worth: Saudi Arabia, Palestine and Malaysia are kin, Turkey and Papua New Guinea affinity, the others bought. Whether this is strategy or drift is the open question in the literature; this card records the structure (low confidence on trend after April 2026, since the Gaza deployment, the overflight request and the J-10 contract are all unresolved as of 12 Oct 2026).

stances.note: Partner, not 'reluctant': China is the first trading partner (USD 167.4bn in 2025, 13th year running), first export market (23.8%), builder of the smelters and the high-speed rail, seller of the J-10 (announced Oct 2025), and Prabowo made Beijing an early destination (Nov 2024, Sept 2025) and received Wang Yi and Dong Jun in Jakarta on 21 Aug 2026. The friction is real - the Natuna 'overlapping claims' formula of 9 Nov 2024 and the Chinese coast guard in the EEZ, the nickel quota fight - but Jakarta has managed it by statement, not by changing the grade; no source describes Indonesia as a reluctant partner, and the structure (a hedger buying from everyone) does not show resistance to alignment that is different from its resistance to every other alignment. Bond - none: pure interest.
